Plătești oamenii înainte de Crăciun? La HMRC treci data din contract.
text:
Multe firme își plătesc oamenii mai repede în decembrie, pentru că atelierul sau biroul se închide în perioada sărbătorilor. Banii pot pleca înainte de termen, dar în raportarea pe care o trimiți la HMRC pentru fiecare plată de salarii — Full Payment Submission — treci data de plată din contract, nu ziua în care banii au ieșit din cont. Exemplul HMRC: plata făcută pe 19 decembrie, data din contract 31 decembrie, se raportează 31 decembrie, iar Full Payment Submission se trimite cel târziu la acea dată. De ce contează: ziua reală, dacă e trecută în raportare, poate aduna două salarii în aceeași perioadă de evaluare pentru Universal Credit și poate micșora sau anula suma pe care angajatul o primește în luna aceea. Dacă plătești la data obișnuită din decembrie, nu ai ce schimba. Dacă data de plată din contract s-a schimbat definitiv, treci data nouă. Și nu este o amânare a taxelor: sumele raportate rămân aceleași, se schimbă doar câmpul datei, iar PAYE și contribuțiile se plătesc tot până pe 22, termenul obișnuit pentru plata electronică.

Notează-ți regula înainte să pregătești salariile din decembrie.

Informații generale. Pentru situația ta, vorbește cu un contabil.

#OlaAccountancy #ValentinTheAccountant #OlaAccountancyLuton #OlaAccountancyBirmingham

alt: Plătești oamenii înainte de Crăciun? La HMRC treci data din contract.
Cadou pentru un client: cel mult 50 de lire, cu reclama firmei pe el.
text:
Vine perioada cadourilor pentru clienți și întrebarea este mereu aceeași: ce pot scădea din profitul pe care îl impozitez? Un cadou pentru un client se scade doar dacă are o reclamă vizibilă a firmei chiar pe el — un pix, o agendă, un mouse pad — și doar dacă totalul cadourilor pentru același client, în perioada contabilă, rămâne sub 50 de lire. Limita se socotește pe client, nu pe fiecare cadou în parte. Cele 50 de lire sunt un prag, nu o primă parte scutită: dacă totalul îl depășește, nu se scade nimic, nici primele 50. Reclama trebuie să fie pe cadou, nu pe ambalaj. Mâncarea, băutura, tutunul și voucherele rămân în afara regulii, oricât ar costa. Nici masa cu clientul nu se scade, oricât de comercială ar fi discuția: orice formă de ospitalitate oferită clienților intră aici, inclusiv cea oferită de angajați sau de un director. Regula de VAT pentru cadouri este o discuție separată, cu alte condiții, iar cadourile pentru angajați și petrecerea de firmă au reguli proprii.

Reține cele 50 de lire înainte să comanzi cadourile pentru clienți.

Informații generale. Pentru situația ta, vorbește cu un contabil.

#OlaAccountancy #ValentinTheAccountant #OlaAccountancyLuton #OlaAccountancyBirmingham

Donezi 100 de lire și plătești impozit de 40%? Ceri 25 de lire de la HMRC.
text:
Ai donat 100 de lire cu Gift Aid și plătești impozit la 40%? Poți primi 25 de lire înapoi, dar numai dacă le ceri tu. Sunt două sume diferite, care vin din două locuri. Prima: cei 25p pentru fiecare liră donată, pe care organizația caritabilă îi cere singură de la HMRC, odată ce ai semnat declarația Gift Aid. A doua: diferența dintre rata la care plătești tu impozit și rata de bază, care se întoarce la tine — și aceasta nu vine singură. O ceri pe declarația de Self Assessment, sau scrii la HMRC și ceri schimbarea tax code-ului, codul după care ți se calculează impozitul pe salariu. Dacă plătești impozit doar la rata de bază, nu primești nimic în plus, pentru că reducerea de impozit a fost deja folosită prin cei 25p ai organizației. Donațiile dintr-un an nu pot depăși de 4 ori impozitul plătit în acel an, iar o declarație Gift Aid are sens doar dacă ai plătit impozit cât să acopere ce recuperează organizația — merită verificat înainte să semnezi una nouă. Unele plăți nu se califică deloc pentru Gift Aid.

Pune deoparte aceste cifre înainte de donațiile de sărbători.

Informații generale. Pentru situația ta, vorbește cu un contabil.

alt: Ring us and you reach the same small team, with your file open.
text:
Ring Ola Accountancy on a Tuesday afternoon and the aim is simple: you start the conversation in the middle, not at the beginning. We are a small team by design and we keep it that way, so the person who picks up is usually the one who did your bookkeeping or filed your last return. They have your business on the screen and they remember what we agreed in September. That matters most on the day you need an answer by four o'clock and you have not got half an hour spare to explain yourself from scratch. A phone call to your accountant should feel like continuing a conversation, not opening a case.

Worth passing to anyone weighing up accountants this winter.

General information. For your own situation, speak to an accountant.

alt: Bring the question you keep putting off.
text:
You know the question. It is the one you nearly asked out loud, or nearly typed into Google at eleven at night, and then left exactly where it was. Bring that one. The first conversation with us is free and lasts half an hour, and it is a conversation rather than a pitch: you say what you do and what is nagging at you, we tell you in plain English what we would look at first and what sorting it would involve. Afterwards you decide. Working with us is one ending; going away to think about it is a perfectly normal one too. We look after businesses in Luton and the towns around it, and plenty more the length of the UK.

Keep this somewhere for the week you decide to get it straightened out.

General information. For your own situation, speak to an accountant.

#OlaAccountancy #ValentinTheAccountant #OlaAccountancyLuton #OlaAccountancyBirmingham

alt: We watch the dates so they stop living in your head.
text:
The best version of this is dull. A short email from us in good time, a list of four things we need from you, you send them over, and some weeks later a line saying it has gone to HMRC with a copy attached. That is the service, and it is meant to be unexciting. We keep the calendar: the yearly accounts a limited company has to file, the VAT returns if you are registered for VAT, the payroll each month, and the Self Assessment tax return, which is due by 31 January. A tax return is just the form that tells HMRC what you earned and what you owe on it. Knowing when each one falls due is the part you are paying us to hold.

One to keep if the dates currently live in your head.

General information. For your own situation, speak to an accountant.

#OlaAccountancy #ValentinTheAccountant #OlaAccountancyLuton #OlaAccountancyBirmingham

alt: It is still, somehow, Friday.
text:
Every business has one. The invoice went out in August and the payment has been going out on Friday ever since. At some point you stopped being annoyed about it and started finding it funny, which is its own kind of warning sign. The uncomfortable part is that an invoice nobody chases quietly turns into a donation. So put the payment date on the invoice itself, send one reminder before that date and one after it, and if it is still sitting there once the date has gone, ring. None of that is aggressive; it is simply what being owed money looks like in a business that is run properly. The people who pay you on time are usually the ones who know you will notice.

alt: Up to £10,500 off the National Insurance you pay on your staff.
text:
If you have people on the payroll, there is up to £10,500 you can take off the National Insurance you pay as their employer in 2026/27. It comes off your employer bill, not off anybody's wages.

And nobody sends it to you. You claim it yourself, through your payroll software, by sending what is called an Employment Payment Summary. The claim also does not roll forward: it has to be made again every tax year, so an employer who claimed last April and assumed it carried on has quietly lost a year of it. The old £100,000 eligibility cap was removed in April 2025.

The employers it does not cover:

— a limited company where the director is the only employee paid above the Secondary Threshold, the point at which employers' National Insurance starts
— a public authority that is not a charity
— an employer with half or more of its work in or for the public sector
— an employer of a nanny, cleaner or gardener, unless that person is a care or support worker
— every company but one in a group of connected companies
— an employer paying a worker under the off-payroll working rules, for those payments

If you run a shop, a garage or a takeaway with three or four on the payroll, it is five minutes of somebody's time to check.

Save this for April, when the claim has to be made all over again.

alt: 25% off the Council Tax bill if you are the only adult at home.
text:
If you are the only adult living in your home, a quarter of your Council Tax bill can come off. That is the single person discount, 25%, and it applies in England and Wales.

It also applies when other adults do live with you and every one of them is, in the council's word, disregarded — someone the rules do not count when they add up the adults in a home. GOV.UK's list includes under-18s, some apprentices, 18 and 19 year olds in full-time education, full-time students, student nurses, live-in carers, people who are severely mentally impaired, and diplomats.

Other reductions sit alongside it. The Disabled Band Reduction Scheme charges the bill at one band lower, or takes 17% off a Band A home where there is no lower band, and it applies only where the home is larger than it would need to be if nobody disabled lived there. Where someone in the home is severely mentally impaired, which is GOV.UK's own term, a discount of 100%, 50% or 25% may apply, depending on who else lives there.

It stops at a second adult. Where two or more adults who are counted live in the property there is no single person discount, and income makes no difference either way: a household with two counted adults does not get it however little it earns. Second homes and long-term empty homes carry a premium instead. Scotland works to its own rules.

Nothing happens automatically. You apply to your own billing authority — Birmingham City Council, or Solihull, Sandwell, Dudley, Walsall, Wolverhampton or Coventry — and you tell them when somebody moves in, because the discount ends from that date.

Save this and check your own bill before the next one lands.

alt: Five ways to work your VAT out from the day's takings.
text:
Black Friday is on Friday. If you run a shop or a takeaway, you are about to put through hundreds of small sales, some with VAT on them and some without, and your till is not going to hand you the VAT on each one.

Where that is genuinely your situation, you are allowed to work the VAT out from a whole day's takings instead. The rules for doing it are the retail schemes, and there are five published ones: point of sale, two apportionment schemes and two direct calculation schemes. Point of sale means the till does the work, rate by rate. The other four work backwards from your takings and from what you bought or sold at each rate.

Three things to know. They are not a saving and they are not the Flat Rate Scheme; they are a way of totalling tax you already owe. For a published scheme there is no application and no permission — you simply use one you are eligible for. And they are only for retailers who cannot account for VAT the normal way, sale by sale: if your till already records the VAT on every sale, HMRC can refuse you a scheme, and can refuse one that does not give a fair and reasonable result.

The size limits. Apportionment scheme 1 and direct calculation scheme 1 are for retail sales, before VAT, of no more than £1 million. The other apportionment and direct calculation schemes run to £130 million. Above £130 million no published scheme is open to you and you agree a tailored one with HMRC.

Some sales never go through a scheme at all. Wholesale and trade sales need normal accounting. Apportionment scheme 1 cannot cover services or goods you made or grew yourself, apportionment scheme 2 cannot cover services or catering, and catering normally goes through point of sale.

Whichever you use, you keep a record of your daily gross takings, and under Making Tax Digital you keep it digitally.

Save this before the weekend, while the till is still quiet.

alt: The bank will only accept the third.
text:
The van says ACE PLUMBING. The invoice says Ace Plumbing & Heating Services. The bank account says a company name somebody registered in 2014 and nobody has said out loud since.

Then a customer goes to pay, their banking app asks them to confirm the name on the account, and it does not match the invoice. So they ring you. You are under a sink. The money waits until Thursday.

It is the least glamorous reason invoices sit unpaid, and it costs nothing to fix. Decide what the business is called. Put that name on the invoice, and put the legal name underneath it where the two differ: your own name if you are a sole trader, or the registered company name and number if you are a limited company. Then make sure the bank account carries a name that matches, because the bank's check is on the account name and nothing else.

One name, three places, one afternoon. It gets you paid faster than any amount of chasing.

alt: No great thing is created suddenly, any more than a bunch of grapes or a fig.
text:
Epictetus was a slave in Rome before he was a philosopher, and he had no patience for the idea that anything worth having arrives finished.

The fig does not negotiate. It takes the time it takes. Blossom, then fruit, then ripening, and skipping a stage is not available.

A business is the same. The client list, the reputation on a street, the accounts that finally make sense — none of it appears in a week. It is built by somebody doing ordinary things repeatedly, in order, for longer than they wanted to.

If you are in the middle of that and it feels slow, it is not a sign you are doing it wrong.

Share this with someone who is building something slowly.

The fig does not negotiate. It takes the time it takes. Blossom, then fruit, then ripening, and skipping a stage is not available.

A business is the same. The client list, the reputation on a street, the accounts that finally make sense — none of it appears in a week. It is built by somebody doing ordinary things repeatedly, in order, for longer than they wanted to.

If you are in the middle of that and it feels slow, it is not a sign you are doing it wrong.

alt: The quietest week is the one where you already know the numbers.
text:
Here is a question that decides how well you sleep: what did the business actually make last month? Most owners cannot answer it without going to look, and the going to look is the bit that never happens.

It is rarely about the size of the business. A one-van operation with current books is calmer than a six-figure one guessing. Three answers do most of the work: what you earned, what is still owed to you, and what is going out before the end of the month. Those three, in front of you, early.

That is most of what we actually do. Not clever schemes. Numbers you can trust, soon enough to change something while it still matters, and someone to talk them through with when they say something you did not expect.

Most people have had the year-end email. An attachment, a lot of columns, a polite line asking you to sign. Nobody reads it, because nobody wrote it to be read.

We do the other thing. We go through your figures with you, out loud, in plain English. Which month was the odd one and why. Where the money actually went, as opposed to where you thought it went. What your margin does when you take the one big client out of the picture. Questions you are allowed to interrupt with, because that is the point of the conversation.

It changes what the numbers are for. A set of accounts filed is a duty. alt: The year directors were given to prove who they are ended 17 November.
text:
If you are a director of a UK company, Companies House now has to know that you are a real, identified person. You prove it once, and what comes back is an 11-character personal code. It belongs to you rather than to a company, and the same code covers every directorship you hold.

What it costs depends entirely on the route. Doing it yourself with Companies House through GOV.UK One Login is free of charge - online, or in person at a participating Post Office with the right documents. There is also a paid route: an authorised provider can verify you instead, and may charge a fee for it. So 'it is free' is true of one route and not the other.

Nobody can do the identity check on your behalf. Companies House says it cannot verify people itself, and an accountant cannot verify you either - once you have your code, your accountant can file using it, but getting it is yours to do.

The code does not then file itself. A director gives it in the company's next confirmation statement. Someone who owns or controls the company gives it through the service for that, inside their own 14-day window. A director of four companies does it four times. If you are both, you do both, separately.

And the timing, because this is the part that has moved. The 12-month transition period for people already on the register started on 18 November 2025 and is over: it ended at the end of 17 November 2026, a week before you are reading this. Companies House says all companies must have met the requirement, or be on a compliance or enforcement pathway, by the end of March 2027. A director who carries on acting unverified is committing an offence, and the first prosecutions have already been through a magistrates' court.

Outside the requirement: shareholders who do not control the company, employees, company secretaries, and sole traders, who are not on the register at all.

Save this if you are a director and that code is still sitting unused.

alt: Owe your own company under £10,000 all year: nothing to report.
text:
Directors take money out of their own company all the time and call it a loan. The line to know is £10,000.

If everything you owe the company, added together, stays under £10,000 for the whole tax year, there is no taxable benefit and nothing to report. An overdrawn director's loan account counts towards it. So does a loan to a relative.

Cross the line and the exemption is gone completely. The benefit is then worked out on the whole loan, not only the part above £10,000, using HMRC's official rate of interest, which is 3.75% from 6 April 2026. And it is tested at any moment in the year, not on the balance sitting there at your year end, so a short spike in the middle of the summer is enough to do it.

One more thing, because it catches people. This is a separate matter from the corporation tax charge on a loan to a participator - somebody with a stake in the company - which has its own rate and its own nine-month repayment rule. One overdrawn account can bring both. The £10,000 has nothing to do with that one.

Outside the £10,000 rule: loans made in place of pay, under salary sacrifice, which have to be reported whatever the balance. Loans already exempt on other grounds do not need the rule at all.

Keep this one to hand before you take the next round out of the company.

alt: So the brown envelope lives on the windowsill.
text:
He set up one address for enquiries, one for invoices, and one he made in a hurry at the bank. Very organised. Three front doors.

He has not opened any of them since the summer. So the things that come on paper instead end up on the windowsill, behind the kettle, going slowly yellow.

This is the most ordinary problem in small business and it is not laziness. Post arrives in four places, so none of them is the place, so nobody checks any of them. The fix is boring and it works: one address that everything points at, one person who opens it, one evening a week. Change it at the bank, at HMRC, at Companies House, on the van.

Nothing that arrives at a company is ever urgent in week one and expensive in week one. It becomes expensive by sitting there.

Share this with whoever has three inboxes and reads none of them.

alt: The cost of a thing is the amount of what I will call life which is required to be exchanged for it.
text:
Thoreau is writing about money, but not in the way people expect. He is saying a price is not really measured in pounds. It is measured in the hours of your life you hand over to earn them.

It is a useful test for a business owner, and an uncomfortable one. The cheap client who takes three times the work is not cheap. The job you took because the number looked good, which then ate your evenings for a month, cost more than it paid. The thing you are putting off because it is boring is quietly charging you interest.

We see this in the numbers more often than people would guess. Revenue up, life down. Those are not the same direction, and only one of them shows on the bank statement.

Save this one and read it again when you next quote a price.
